The meshwarp vertex data can be output as a matrix via the output_mesh_matrix message.
Texture output is enabled via the output_texture attribute. When enabled the meshwarp is rendered to an internal texture and output from the leftmost outlet
jit.gl.meshwarp supports both texture and matrix output.
You can use masks to mask portions of the jit.gl.meshwarp plane.

1 - Enable "mask_mode".
2 - Press "shift" and double click inside the plane.  
3 - Click and drag with the mouse on the yellow dots to move masks vertices. 
4 - Press "ctrl (win) / cmd (mac)" + drag the blue dot to move the mask around the scene.
5 - Press "shift" and double click on the edges of the masks to create new vertices.
6 - Press "shift" and double click on a yellow dot to delete a mask vertex. 
7 - Press "shift" and double click on the blue dot to delete a whole mask.

8 - Enable "apply_mask" to apply the mask to the plane.
9 - You can invert the mask with the "invert_mask 1/0" message.
10 - Send the "reset_mask" message to reset all masks.
11 - Disable "mask_mode" to go back to editing the jit.gl.meshwarp mesh.

Each json file describes a single jit.gl.meshwarp configuration. These messages referencing meshwarpA and meshwarpB are sent to the meshwarp objects in the "multiple meshwarps" tab.

Save all the parameters of a jit.gl.meshwarp in a JSON file using the "write" message. To bring the object back to its saved state, load the JSON file into the jit.gl.meshwarp object with the "read" message.

In the jit.world window, perform these actions:
You can alter the projected image by moving specific points in the mesh.

- Blue Circle: click and drag the blue circle in the center of the mesh to move the entire mesh.
- Yellow Circles: click and drag the yellow circles at the edges of the mesh to scale it. 
- Red Circles: When you hover over an individual vertex a red circle appears. Click and drag a red circle to move an individual vertex.
- Click and Drag: select multiple vertices by clicking and dragging over an area of the mesh. After selecting the vertices you can move them all in bulk by clicking and dragging on a selected vertex.
